results.title: Nebius hikes AI cloud prices again as demand for computing power soars | My 95.7
results.author: Thomson Reuters
highlights:
Sept 17 (Reuters) – Cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected ​Nvidia chips from October 1, ‌marking the company’s second price hike in three months.

Demand for computing capacity to train and run AI models is surging; rival CoreWeave ‌said ​earlier in the ⁠day that it is ⁠signing contracts at higher prices.

Here are some details:

• Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between ​17% and 21%.

• On-demand rates for some central processing units, made ⁠by AMD and Intel, ⁠and memory offerings have also ​been hiked.

• Prices of some CPU-only instances ​will rise by 25% and those ‌of memory offerings by about 41%, the company said.

• The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm said that customers reserving large-scale clusters ⁠for multiple months can receive commitment discounts.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

Ask about locking today's rate. Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate. Get the answer in writing, with the rate and term.

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

If you are planning a project, get a dated quote for your actual start date. Ask what a 3, 6 or 12 month commitment costs against the new on demand rate. Ask whether that commitment reserves GPUs or only lowers the rate.

results.title: Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Pricing Across H100, H200
results.author: MarketCatalyst Desk
highlights:
Nebius will raise on-demand GPU cloud pricing across H100, H200, B200 and B300 starting October 1, as it scales capacity and secures financing tied to deployed GPUs.

...

Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) is planning to raise prices on several of its on-demand GPU, CPU, and memory services starting October 1, according to a customer pricing notice reviewed by MarketCatalyst. The adjustments touch the company's most sought-after compute tiers — NVIDIA's H100, H200, B200, and B300 chips — and follow a strong second quarter shaped by rising AI Cloud demand.

...

## What's Changing

The notice lists new per-GPU-hour rates across four NVIDIA chip families, plus adjustments to underlying CPU and memory pricing:

| Hardware | New Rate | Previous Rate | Region(s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 | $4.50 / GPU-hr | $3.85 / GPU-hr | eu-north1 |
| NVIDIA H200 | $5.40 / GPU-hr | $4.50 / GPU-hr | Listed European & U.S. regions |
| NVIDIA B200 | $8.50 / GPU-hr | $7.15 / GPU-hr | us-central1, me-west1 |
| NVIDIA B300 | $9.50 / GPU-hr | $7.85 / GPU-hr | uk-south1, eu-west2, us-north1 |

The increases range from roughly 15% for the H100 and H200 to about 21% for the B300, which sees the largest adjustment of the four. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory rates are also moving slightly higher as part of the same notice, while Intel Ice Lake CPU pricing remains unchanged.

The bottom line

Every chip seeing a price increase is a current-generation or near-current NVIDIA accelerator used for AI training and inference, rather than older, lower-demand hardware. This pattern is consistent with a company adjusting prices where capacity is tightest, rather than where it may be trying to move idle inventory.

...

The rate changes are set to take effect October 1 across the regions listed above. Customers with existing reserved or contracted capacity commitments are typically governed by separate contract terms rather than these on-demand list prices, though the notice offers a useful signal on the broader direction of AI compute costs as capacity remains tight across the industry.

...

### When do Nebius's new GPU prices take effect?

According to a customer pricing notice, the new rates for H100, H200, B200, and B300 GPUs, along with AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory pricing, are set to take effect October 1.

...

H100 pricing in eu-north1 is set to rise to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85. H200 pricing is set to rise to $5.40 per GPU-hour from $4.50 across listed European and U.S. regions. B200 pricing in us-central1 and me-west1 is set to rise to $8.50 from $7.15 per GPU-hour. B300 pricing in uk-south1, eu-west2, and us-north1 is set to rise to $9.50 from $7.85 per GPU-hour.

results.title: Nebius lifts the H100 to $4.50 an hour while Burry loads the short · The Inference
results.author: Vincent Jiang
highlights:
From 1 October, an hour on a 2022-vintage H100 rents for $4.50↗ on Nebius▼−12.27% — Nebius, down 12.27 percent today, up from $3.85, the second round of on-demand increases since 1 June↗ 1 3 5. Charging more each quarter for four-year-old silicon is either the strongest demand signal in the AI trade or its last tick, and both camps have money down.

...

## The list price is a ceiling

The customer notice, reported 16 September, lifts the whole menu: H200 to $5.40 from $4.50, B200 to $8.50 from $7.15, B300 to $9.50 from $7.85, rises of 17 to 21 percent 1 3. The public page still carried only the old rates when the news broke; by 27 September it posted both columns, current and "Effective October 1, 2026"↗ 3 8. Commitment discounts run up to 35 percent below on-demand↗, so the menu is a ceiling, not an average 3 8.

Second-quarter revenue was $582.3 million, up 454 percent, at a 41 percent adjusted-EBITDA margin↗ 1 6. The list is a peak price: spot H100s start at $0.79 an hour↗, and even with the October rise counted the menu sits near half of AWS rates 5 8.

results.title: Nebius raises prices across the board: GPU leasing increases… | Longbridge
results.author: Zhitong
highlights:
In a notice sent to customers (which was shared by Reddit and X users), Nebius announced that it would increase the prices of several on-demand computing resources starting October 1, with the latest NVIDIA GPUs seeing the largest price hikes.

Under the new prices, the H100 will rise from $3.85/GPU hour to $4.50/GPU hour, an increase of about 17%; the H200 will go from $4.50 to $5.40, a 20% increase; the B200 will increase from $7.15 to $8.50, nearly a 19% rise; and the NVIDIA B300 will see the largest absolute increase, from $7.85 to $9.50/GPU hour, approximately a 21% increase.

results.title: Nebius raises on-demand GPU prices from 1 October | VETTDD
results.author: Editor Editorial desk, VETTDD
highlights:
- Spot prices for preemptible HGX H100 and H200 instances start from $0.79 (£0.60) per GPU-hour, and Nebius says they can change as often as every 15 minutes.
- Nebius’s pricing FAQ gives US dollars as the only currency it accepts.
- Egress and ingress traffic, public IP addresses and Nebius’s managed Kubernetes service are listed as free.

...

Nebius will charge more for on-demand graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity from 1 October 2026, according to the price list on its website. An Nvidia HGX H100 instance rises from $3.85 (£2.91) to $4.50 (£3.40) per GPU-hour, and an HGX B300 from $7.85 (£5.93) to $9.50 (£7.17).

The rest of the HGX range moves the same way. H200 goes from $4.50 to $5.40 (£4.08) and B200 from $7.15 (£5.40) to $8.50 (£6.42). On the page’s own figures, the four rises run from 17% to 21%. Central processing unit (CPU) instances go up too, with AMD Epyc Genoa starting at $0.13 (£0.10) an hour instead of $0.10. RTX Pro 6000 and L40S prices are unchanged, and the rack-scale GB300 and GB200 NVL72 systems remain price on request.
